q: How should an engineering unit near Rourkela count the steel it buys from the plant or its stockyards?
title: Rourkela ancillaries: steel in Scope 3
short: Steel bought is Scope 3, Category 1, purchased goods: tonnes from your invoices multiplied by a per tonne figure for that product. Ask the stockyard or the plant for the plant's product figure; if you only have a route average for blast furnace steel, use it, name the source and mark it as an estimate.
audience: Fabrication, structural and engineering MSMEs in the Rourkela and Kalunga industrial estates

ol: Total tonnes by product from purchase invoices.
Get a plant figure per tonne, or a stated average.
Multiply and keep the source next to the number.

p: For a fabricator, bought steel is usually far bigger than its own electricity and fuel. A buyer asking for your footprint will look here first.

sections.h: If you export to the EU
p: Fabricated structures under CN 7308 are CBAM goods. Your own figure then carries the steel as a precursor, and default values apply if you cannot get the mill figure.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so each figure in a CBAM or buyer response can be traced back to the documents behind it.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
